chunks: From him, from Zur‘ah, from Samā‘ah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning:

Regarding a Muslim man who kills a man from the People of the Covenant, he said: “This is a severe hadith which people cannot bear; but the dhimmī gives the blood-money of the Muslim, then the Muslim is killed for him.”

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: non-Muslim subjects living under covenant and protection
key_terms.حَدِيثٌ شَدِيدٌ: a severe or weighty ruling that is difficult for people to accept
key_terms.دِيَةَ: blood-money paid in compensation for unlawful killing
key_terms.يُقْتَلُ بِهِ: is killed in retaliation for him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām on a Muslim who kills a dhimmī?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a legal ruling concerning retaliation in the case of a Muslim who kills a dhimmī. It describes the matter as severe and difficult for people to bear, while stating that the blood-money of a Muslim is to be given and then the Muslim is executed in retaliation.
